title: Special Topics in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies; Gender and Sports
description: Students examine athletic culture as an arena where gender, race, and sexuality are simultaneously produced, policed, and contested. Drawing on feminist theory, masculinity studies, and the cultural study of sport, we ask how bodies come to matter in athletic spaces and whose bodies arecelebrated, scrutinized, or excluded. Throughout this course, students will develop tools for analyzing sport as a social institution embedded in histories of colonialism, capitalism, sexism, and racism. This coursewill move across scales, from legal codes to bodily practicesto cultural mythology to trace how gender operates through seemingly neutral rules, scientific claims, and everyday traditions. By centering figures,policies, and moments that reveal the uneven terrain of athleticlife, we use sport as a lens through which to understand broaderstructures of power.
